title: Space Whiskers: The Holy Cow
tagline: Pip, a mouse astronaut, in the cats' shipyard: a test level for his animations
description: The first playable piece of the Space Whiskers remake: Pip at the game's own scale (49 pixels tall, on a 480 x 270 screen) runs and jumps through a corner of the Whiskerworks shipyard, so his animations, the controls and the light can be judged in motion. Decks, crates, catwalks, a scaffold tower and a long run to the cheese; lamps that cast shadows, and test lights you can drop anywhere.
controls: drop a test light (right click takes the nearest away)
kind of test light: warm, cold, spot, alarm
a light that follows the mouse
stick or d-pad, A jump, X or B sprint, Y walk

speed.label: Move speed
speed.help: Pip's normal speed in game pixels a second (he is 49 tall, the screen 480 wide): three Pips a second. His run drawings play at this pace.

sprintSpeed.label: Sprint speed
sprintSpeed.help: His top speed while the sprint button is held.

walkSpeed.label: Walk speed
walkSpeed.help: His speed while the walk key (C) is held: the walk drawings, a slow, careful pace. Below about 100 pixels a second the walk is what is drawn.

accelTime.label: Time to full speed
accelTime.help: How long he takes from standing to his top speed: lower is snappier.

stopTime.label: Time to stop
stopTime.help: How long he takes to stop (and to turn round) when you let go.

jumpHeight.label: Jump height
jumpHeight.help: How high a full jump lifts his feet (hold the button; let go early for a short hop). 80 is about one and two thirds Pips.

jumpTime.label: Time to the top
jumpTime.help: How long a full jump takes to reach its top: lower is snappier (the game works out the gravity from this and the height).

airControl.label: Air control
airControl.help: How well he steers in the air, as a share of his control on the ground.

walkStride.label: Walk stride
walkStride.help: How far he moves for each frame of the walk: the animation is driven by distance, so his boots keep pace with the floor at any speed.

screenWidth.label: Screen width
screenWidth.help: How many game pixels the view is wide (480 x 270 is the agreed screen); the window is filled in whole device pixels.
